title: Failure patterns: how agents overclaim, and how to catch it
summary: Drake has catalogued how agents overclaim: receipts with no artifact, runners that silently lose cases so the pass rate looks perfect, NOT_RUN counted as PASS, a compile taken as proof of behavior, merged called deployed, and a lead restoring a model setting before its child agent started. Each has a mechanical check. I can run his tally program that counts PASS, FAIL and NOT_RUN against the case count fixed before the run.
goal: Recognize the common ways agent reports overclaim and put a mechanical check in front of each.
key_steps: Require an artifact for every claim of done, PASS, merged or measured
Fix the expected case count before the run
Treat fewer results than expected as a failure
Report NOT_RUN and SKIP as not passed
Run the changed path and a negative control, not just the compile
Confirm a child agent's model from its own session record

example.code:
note tally: count PASS, FAIL and NOT_RUN in a runner log against the case count fixed before the run
note exit 0 every expected case passed, 1 not a pass, 2 read error, 3 no expected count (fail closed)
text KW "expect \nPASS \nFAIL \nNOT_RUN \nSKIP \nexpected=\n results=\n pass=\n fail=\nSHRUNK: denominator lost \n case(s): they produced no result, so they did not pass\nGREW: unexpected results=\n (the case list changed: re-pin it before trusting a rate)\nNOT_RUN or SKIP=\n (NOT_RUN is not PASS)\nREFUSE: no expected case count, so no pass rate can be trusted\n not_run=\n noise=\n\nVERDICT PASS\nVERDICT FAIL\n"
note helpers: read all of stdin into inb, walk lines, compare a line prefix with the n-th
note entry of the newline separated table KW, and write table entries, input bytes and numbers
global inb uchar 65536
global num uchar 24
fn rdall to long
t = ulong 0
while lt t len inb bound 65536
k = read 0 inb t sub len inb t
if lt k 0
ret k
end
if eq k 0
ret long t
end
t = add t ulong k
end
ret neg long 27
end
fn eol s ulong n ulong to ulong
i = s
while lt i n bound 65536
if eq get inb i 10
ret i
end
i = add i 1
end
ret n
end
fn kstart k ulong to ulong
p = ulong 0
c = ulong 0
while lt c k bound 4096
if eq get KW p 10
c = add c 1
end
p = add p 1
end
ret p
end
fn klen k ulong to ulong
s = kstart k
i = s
while ne get KW i 10 bound 4096
i = add i 1
end
ret sub i s
end
fn pmat at ulong e ulong k ulong to bool
o = kstart k
m = klen k
if gt m sub e at
ret false
end
for j ulong m
if ne get inb add at j get KW add o j
ret false
end
end
ret true
end
fn emitk o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 4096
w = write 1 KW add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn emiti o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 65536
w = write 1 inb add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn emitn o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 24
w = write 1 num add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn say k ulong to void
emitk kstart k add klen k 1
end
fn word k ulong to void
emitk kstart k klen k
end
fn emitu v ulong to void
p = ulong 24
x = v
while true bound 21
p = sub p 1
put num p uchar add rem x 10 48
x = div x 10
if eq x 0
break
end
end
emitn p sub 24 p
end
note the first line is: expect N (the case count fixed before the run)
note then PASS name, FAIL name, NOT_RUN name or SKIP name per case; other lines are runner noise
global cnt ulong 5
fn expn s ulong e ulong to ulong
if not pmat s e 0
ret 0
end
v = ulong 0
i = add s klen 0
if ge i e
ret 0
end
while lt i e bound 7
c = get inb i
if lt c 48
ret 0
end
if gt c 57
ret 0
end
v = add mul v 10 ulong sub c 48
i = add i 1
if gt sub i s 12
ret 0
end
end
ret v
end
fn kind s ulong e ulong to ulong
for k ulong 4
if pmat s e add k 1
if eq k 3
ret 2
end
ret k
end
end
ret 3
end
fn shout k ulong v ulong to void
word k
emitu v
end
fn flags x ulong m ulong to void
if lt m x
shout 9 sub x m
say 10
end
if gt m x
shout 11 sub m x
say 12
end
if gt get cnt 2 0
shout 13 get cnt 2
say 14
end
end
fn main to int
r = rdall
if lt r 0
ret 2
end
n = ulong r
e = eol 0 n
x = expn 0 e
if eq x 0
say 15
ret 3
end
s = add e 1
while lt s n bound 65536
e = eol s n
k = kind s e
put cnt k add get cnt k 1
s = add e 1
end
m = add add get cnt 0 get cnt 1 get cnt 2
shout 5 x
shout 6 m
shout 7 get cnt 0
shout 8 get cnt 1
shout 16 get cnt 2
shout 17 get cnt 3
say 18
flags x m
if eq get cnt 0 x
if eq m x
say 19
ret 0
end
end
say 20
ret 1
end

common_mistake: Trusting a runner's '0 failed' summary. It is true in every failing log of the example. Fix: compare results against a pre-fixed expected count and fail closed on any gap.
evidence_note: The example ran on a Linux AArch64 host (no GPU) and its output is recorded byte for byte with a negative control. Rests on the recorded run of tally.om: a full log passes; shrunk, NOT_RUN and uncounted logs fail (exit 1 or 3) although all have zero FAIL lines. NOT done: this is a teaching checker, not any repository's gate.
